*Proof.* For $|\zeta|=1$, $E_\zeta=I-D/\zeta$ is invertible and $$E_\zeta^*\Phi_D(\zeta)E_\zeta=I-D^*D\succeq0.$$

Let $k\ge1$, and let $F=F_\Omega\circ G$ be $M_k$-valued, with $F_\Omega$ holomorphic near $\overline\Omega$ and $\|F(t)\|\le1$ on $\mathbb T$. Suppose $p,q,r\in\mathcal H_k$ satisfy $$p=p^*,\quad q=q^*,\quad p=F^*r,\quad q=rF^*,\quad
 r_0=0,\quad\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(p_0)>0.$$ For a positive number $\kappa$, define $$p_e=\mathcal C^\dagger p+\widetilde\mathcal C^\dagger p,\qquad
 q_e=\mathcal C^\dagger q+\widetilde\mathcal C^\dagger q,\qquad
 r_e=\kappa\mathcal C^\dagger r+\kappa^{-1}\widetilde\mathcal C^\dagger r.$$ If the $2k$-by-$2k$ block $$\Delta(t)=\begin{pmatrix}p_e(t)&r_e(t)^*\\r_e(t)&q_e(t)\end{pmatrix}
 \succeq0$$ for almost every $t\in\mathbb T$, then $\kappa\le2$.

outputs.exact_statement: For every admissible $\Omega$ there is a conformal bijection $f:\Omega\to\mathbb D$ such that $f$ and $f^{-1}$ extend univalently through $\overline\Omega$ and $\overline\mathbb D$, respectively. There is also a conformal bijection $G:\{|t|>1\}\to\mathbb C\setminus\overline\Omega$ that extends univalently to $\{|t|>r\}\cup\{\infty\}$ for some $0<r<1$, as a sphere map, with a simple pole at infinity and $G(\mathbb T)=\partial\Omega$. On $\mathbb T$, $tG'(t)$ is an outward normal and $\psi=f\circ G$ is an orientation-preserving smooth circle diffeomorphism.

For every admissible $\Omega$, every finite $n\ge1$, every $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ with $W(A)\subset\Omega$, and the interior conformal coordinate $f$ above, the problem [eq:minimum] is strictly feasible and has an attained minimum $1\le\kappa^2\le4$. If $H$ is a minimizing metric, then $$S=H^{1/2},\qquad A'=SAS^{-1},\qquad D=Sf(A)S^{-1}=f(A')$$ satisfy $$D^*D\preceq I,\qquad \rho(D)<1, \qquad \|S\|\|S^{-1}\|=\kappa\le2.$$

With the same $\Omega,A,f,G$ and any chosen minimizing metric in Theorem 2, there is one continuous function $\Lambda:\mathbb T\to M_n(\mathbb C)$ satisfying $$\Lambda(t)\succeq0,\qquad \int_\mathbb T\Lambda(t)\,d\sigma(t)=I_n,$$ such that, for every positive integer $m$ and every $M_m(\mathbb C)$-valued function $v$ holomorphic on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$, $$\label{eq:representation-target} v[A']=\int_\mathbb T\Lambda(t)\otimes v(G(t))\,d\sigma(t), \qquad \|v[A]\|\le\kappa\max_{\overline\Omega}\|v\|.$$ The same $S$, $\Lambda$, and $\kappa$ work for all $m$ and $v$.

If $\kappa>1$, there are $X,Y\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ with $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(XX^*)=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(YY^*)=1,\qquad SX=\kappa X,\qquad SY=Y,
 \qquad X^*Y=0,$$ and an $M_n$-valued rational function $F_\mathbb D$, holomorphic on a neighborhood of $\overline\mathbb D$ and contractive on $\overline\mathbb D$, such that, for $x=\mathop{\mathrm{vec}}(X)$ and $y=\mathop{\mathrm{vec}}(Y)$, $$F_\mathbb D[D]x=y.$$ In particular $F_\Omega=F_\mathbb D\circ f$ is holomorphic near $\overline\Omega$ and satisfies $F_\Omega[A']x=y$. Its boundary trace $F=F_\Omega\circ G$ is contractive.

Let $k\ge1$, and let $F=F_\Omega\circ G$ be $M_k$-valued, with $F_\Omega$ holomorphic near $\overline\Omega$ and $\|F(t)\|\le1$ on $\mathbb T$. Suppose $p,q,r\in\mathcal H_k$ satisfy $$p=p^*,\quad q=q^*,\quad p=F^*r,\quad q=rF^*,\quad
 r_0=0,\quad\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(p_0)>0.$$ For a positive number $\kappa$, define $$p_e=\mathcal C^\dagger p+\widetilde\mathcal C^\dagger p,\qquad
 q_e=\mathcal C^\dagger q+\widetilde\mathcal C^\dagger q,\qquad
 r_e=\kappa\mathcal C^\dagger r+\kappa^{-1}\widetilde\mathcal C^\dagger r.$$ If the $2k$-by-$2k$ block $$\Delta(t)=\begin{pmatrix}p_e(t)&r_e(t)^*\\r_e(t)&q_e(t)\end{pmatrix}
 \succeq0$$ for almost every $t\in\mathbb T$, then $\kappa\le2$.

For every pair of positive integers $n,m$, every $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$, every nonnegative integer $d$, and every choice of matrices $B_0,\ldots,B_d\in M_m(\mathbb C)$, the polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^dB_jz^j$ satisfies $$\|P[A]\|=\left\|\sum_{j=0}^dA^j\otimes B_j\right\|
 \le2\max_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|.$$ The constant is independent of both matrix sizes and the degree. No smaller constant holds uniformly over these choices.

For every nonempty compact convex $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ and every $\epsilon>0$, there is an admissible $\Omega_\epsilon$ such that $$K\subset\Omega_\epsilon,\qquad
 \overline\Omega_\epsilon\subset\{x:\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(x,K)<\epsilon\}.$$

Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space, with no separability assumption, and let $A\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Suppose first that $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$, and put $$W(A)=\{\langle x,Ax\rangle:x\in\mathcal H,\ \|x\|=1\},
 \qquad K=\overline{W(A)}.$$ Then $K$ is compact and convex and contains $\mathop{\mathrm{spec}}(A)$. For every positive integer $m$, every nonnegative integer $d$, and every matrix polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^d B_kz^k$ with $B_k\in M_m(\mathbb C)$, the operator $P[A]=\sum_{k=0}^d A^k\otimes B_k$ on $\mathcal H\otimes\mathbb C^m$ satisfies $$\label{eq:hilbert-polynomial}
 \|P[A]\|\le 2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|
             =2\max_{z\in K}\|P(z)\|.$$ More generally, if $U$ is an open neighborhood of $K$ and $F=(f_{ij}):U\to M_m(\mathbb C)$ is holomorphic, its entrywise holomorphic evaluation, in the same base-first tensor convention, satisfies $$\label{eq:hilbert-holomorphic}
 F[A]:=\sum_{i,j=1}^m f_{ij}(A)\otimes E_{ij},
 \qquad \|F[A]\|\le2\max_{z\in K}\|F(z)\|.$$ Here $E_{ij}$ are the standard matrix units and $f_{ij}(A)$ is given by the holomorphic functional calculus. In particular, $K$ is a complete $2$-spectral set for $A$: the same estimate holds at every finite coefficient size for every matrix-valued rational function whose poles lie outside $K$, with evaluation by the rational functional calculus. The constant two is optimal uniformly over all these choices.*

*If $\mathcal H=\{0\}$, every evaluation is the zero operator. With the supremum over the empty numerical range defined to be zero, the corresponding supremum-norm inequalities are $0\le0$; the compact spectral-set assertion above is stated for nonzero $\mathcal H$.
